feedback: Judged from earlier races only. Iteration 2 (kp 8.0, kd 0.2, ki 0.0) is the best raced design at score 49.78, with progress 0.18 on the oval, 0.10 on the s-bend and 0.085 on the slalom. Iterations 0 and 1 (kp 5.0) stalled at progress 0.04 to 0.125. Iteration 2 also raised steering_oscillation to 0.13 to 0.15 on every track (0.15 on the oval), and max_error stayed at about 0.066 on the oval, so the robot still leaves the 0.06 m band. This candidate changes one group only, kp from 8.0 to 6.0. Geometry, base_speed, ki, kd and line_loss are unchanged, so the race isolates the gain step. Every field is inside its contract range. I state no outcome for this candidate. Approve because it is a clean, single-group test of the overshoot diagnosis, and a race is needed to learn whether the 0.15 oscillation or the progress gain matters more. Next race: (a) if steering_oscillation falls near 0.10 and progress holds at or above the kp 8 level, keep kp near 6 and move to sensor geometry. (b) If progress drops clearly below the kp 8 level (oval below about 0.15), return to kp 7.0 and keep kd 0.2, since the gain is the main source of progress. (c) If progress stalls at a fixed point with low oscillation, the sensor dead band around the centre sensor (0.012 m sensors, 0.02 m spacing, 0.025 m tape) is the likely cause, so change sensor_size to 0.016 next. (d) If the robot tracks the line but completion_time exceeds 3 s, raise base_speed to 1.6. Change one group per revision.
